chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Shuʿayb, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I said to him: People narrate that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days of the month of Ramaḍān more often than he fasted thirty.

He said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except completely, and the obligatory acts are not deficient. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the year as three hundred and sixty days, and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, so He withheld them from the three hundred and sixty days; thus the year is three hundred and fifty-four days. And the month of Ramaḍān is thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
and that you complete the number
And that which is complete is full. And Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, and Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights
So the month is thus and then thus, meaning: one month complete and one month deficient. And the month of Ramaḍān never diminishes, and Shaʿbān is never complete.

key_terms.السَّنَةَ: the year, whose number of days is discussed in the report
key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: the prescribed number to be completed, cited from the Qur'an
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضُ: the obligatory religious duties, described here as not being deficient
key_terms.الْكَامِلُ: that which is complete or full, used to explain the verse
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the month of fasting under discussion in the narration
key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: the month mentioned as never being complete in this report
key_terms.شَوَّالٌ: the month mentioned as having twenty-nine days in this report

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith state that the month of Ramaḍān is always thirty days and never deficient?
ai.summary: This hadith reports from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام a ruling concerning the number of days in the month of Ramaḍān, rejecting reports that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted it as twenty-nine days more often than thirty. It also cites Qur'anic phrases to support the completeness of the count and presents a pattern for the lunar months in which Ramaḍān remains complete.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2042 - In a narration from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi’, from Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Shu’ayb, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (as), he said:
"I said to him: 'People narrate that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) fasted for 29 days in the Month of Ramadan more often than he fasted for 30 days.'
Imam (as) replied: 'They have lied. The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) only fasted a complete month. 
Obligatory acts are never deficient. Verily, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, created the year with 360 days and created the heavens and the earth in six days, thus reducing the days of the year to 354.
The Month of Ramadan is 30 days, as Allah (swt), the Almighty, says: "And complete the number" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185). Completeness means perfection.
Shawwal is 29 days, and Dhu al-Qa'dah is 30 days, as Allah (swt), the Almighty, says:
"And We appointed for Musa thirty nights" (Surah Al-A’raf 7:142).
The months alternate in this way - one complete month, followed by a deficient one. The Month of Ramadan is never deficient, and Sha’ban is never complete.'"
